newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PICKS GASOLINE AS FIRST OIL FUTURES LISTING.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PICKS GASOLINE AS FIRST OIL FUTURES LISTING.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said on Monday that gasoline is likely to debut as the exchange's first-ever energy futures contract in 1999, instead of a basket of Middle Eastern and regional crude grades.
"Since it takes time for a crude basket to be acknowledged by market players, gasoline is going to be listed first," said Mitsuhiro Onosato, general manager of TOCOM's planning department.

Onosato, architect of the proposed Tokyo-based oil futures contracts, said earlier this year that TOCOM would list either gasoline or a basket of crude grades in the business year starting in April 1999.
Details of the contract, such as lot sizes and delivery methods and locations, will be mapped out by October, he said.
TOCOM also aims eventually to list gas oil and kerosene contracts, but only after a successful launch of the gasoline futures contract, Onosato added.
The Chubu Commodity Exchange in Nagoya, central Japan, said last week it plans to list gasoline, gas oil and kerosene contracts concurrently, as early as 1999.

The contracts are likely to be yen-denominated and one lot is expected to be equivalent to 10 kilolitres, Hideaki Nakamura, head of the exchange's planning department, said. He added that the exchange is unlikely to list crude oil.
